feedback.problem: Let $u$ and $v$ be vectors such that $‖u‖=15$ and $‖u+\sqrt{5}v‖=75.$  If $u$ is orthogonal to $v$, find $‖v‖.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u$ is orthogonal to $v,$ we also have that $u$ is orthogonal to $\sqrt{5}v.$ So, the Pythagorean theorem states that

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u+\sqrt{5}v{‖}^{2} & =‖u{‖}^{2}+‖\sqrt{5}v{‖}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying and substituting in the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u+\sqrt{5}v{‖}^{2} & =‖u{‖}^{2}+(\sqrt{5}‖v‖)^{2} \\ ‖u+\sqrt{5}v{‖}^{2} & =‖u{‖}^{2}+5‖v{‖}^{2} \\ (75)^{2} & =(15)^{2}+5‖v{‖}^{2} \\ 5\,625 & =225+5‖v{‖}^{2} \\ 5\,400 & =5‖v{‖}^{2} \\ ‖v{‖}^{2} & =1\,080\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $‖v‖=6\sqrt{30}.$
